_comment: Deterministic fixtures for the multi-type question evaluator (TASK-2301, Phase P1).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Evaluation has to run offline (Practice/Mock Test work fully
signed out) and also has to be correct for a signed-in student's server-computed
history, so the evaluator is implemented twice on purpose - in Java
(backend/.../evaluation/SingleChoiceEvaluator.java) and in TypeScript
(packages/core/src/evaluation/questionEvaluator.ts) - the same duplication precedent
used for the Weakness Radar's topic-health algorithm, and this file follows that one's
shape deliberately.
BOTH sides now assert against this file: Java in QuestionEvaluatorsTest, TypeScript in
packages/core/src/evaluation/questionEvaluator.test.ts (Vitest, added by TASK-2601
Phase 0 when the evaluator moved into the shared package). Until then the TypeScript
copy genuinely had no test runner and was verified by reading; that caveat is now
obsolete and should not be reintroduced. A case added here must hold on both sides.
Phase P2 Wave A (V26) added MULTIPLE_CHOICE and TRUE_FALSE cases below - both genuinely
new evaluators (set equality, boolean equality). ASSERTION_REASON and
STATEMENT_COMBINATION need no cases of their own: both reuse SingleChoiceEvaluator
unchanged (see QuestionEvaluators.java), so the SINGLE_CHOICE cases above already cover
their evaluation logic - only their authored content differs, which the evaluator never
sees.
Phase P2 Wave B (V27) added NUMERIC/FILL_BLANK/MATCH/ORDERING cases below - four more
genuinely new evaluators (tolerance comparison, case-insensitive text match, map
equality, list equality).
A constants-parity script (the pattern check-topic-health-parity.js already proved) is
still deliberately NOT added: NUMERIC's tolerance is per-question authored data (stored
in answerKey), not a shared constant either side could drift on independently - there is
still nothing here for such a script to check.
Phase P4 (schema-only, no student UI) added ManualEvaluator/manualEvaluator for the
MANUAL family (SHORT_ANSWER, LONG_ANSWER) - a descriptive answer can never be scored by
comparison, so every attempted response evaluates to PENDING_REVIEW rather than
CORRECT/INCORRECT, awaiting a human reviewer this phase does not build. Cases below are
tagged LONG_ANSWER only; SHORT_ANSWER shares the exact same evaluator instance and needs
no cases of its own, the same reasoning ASSERTION_REASON/STATEMENT_COMBINATION already
established for reusing SingleChoiceEvaluator above.

cases.name: first-option-can-be-correct
cases.why: The old client-side fallback (mobile/src/db/answerResolution.ts's resolveCorrectIndex) defaults an unparseable answer to index 0 with a warning, which has historically hidden bugs where 0 looked like a legitimate correct answer. This case pins that 0 is a perfectly ordinary correct index, not a special or suspicious one.

cases.name: no-response-is-unattempted-not-incorrect
cases.why: A skipped question must never be scored the same as a wrong pick - see TopicEvidenceRepository's own comment on excluding unattempted mock rows from the Weakness Radar for the same reason.

cases.name: missing-response-object-is-unattempted
cases.why: A response of null (never wrote anything) must behave identically to an explicit null selectedOption - both mean 'nothing recorded', not two different states.

cases.name: multiple-choice-exact-set-match-scores-1
cases.why: Order must not matter - the student ticked the same set in a different scan order.

cases.name: multiple-choice-partial-overlap-scores-0
cases.why: All-or-nothing (architecture proposal open question 2) - two of three correct options ticked still scores 0, matching how these exams actually grade multi-select.

cases.name: multiple-choice-extra-wrong-pick-scores-0
cases.why: Every correct option ticked, PLUS a wrong one - still all-or-nothing, not 'mostly right'.

cases.name: multiple-choice-empty-selection-is-attempted-not-unattempted
cases.why: Ticking nothing and submitting is a real, scoreable wrong answer, distinct from never engaging with the question at all (selectedOptions: null below).

cases.name: true-false-correct-false
cases.why: False must be an ordinary correct answer, not treated as a default/unset-like value the way a careless falsy check could.

cases.name: numeric-within-tolerance-scores-1
cases.why: A tolerance of 0.5 must accept anything within it, not just an exact match.

cases.name: fill-blank-case-and-whitespace-insensitive-match-scores-1
cases.why: A real short-answer field can't require byte-exact input - trimming and case-folding both sides is what makes 'new delhi' and 'New Delhi' the same answer.

cases.name: fill-blank-blank-entry-is-unattempted
cases.why: A student who typed only whitespace and submitted hasn't really answered - same rule as never touching the field.

cases.name: match-one-pair-wrong-scores-0
cases.why: All-or-nothing, same rule as MULTIPLE_CHOICE - one wrong pair among several correct ones still scores 0.

cases.name: ordering-adjacent-swap-scores-0
cases.why: Order genuinely matters - the same three items in a different sequence is a wrong answer, not a near-miss.

cases.name: manual-entry-is-pending-review
cases.why: A descriptive answer can never be auto-scored - a real attempt evaluates to PENDING_REVIEW, not CORRECT/INCORRECT, since only a human reviewer (not built this phase) can say whether it's right.

response.enteredText: The Quit India Movement began in August 1942.
